input:
This memo recommends a three-month pilot on 17 pumps before any decision on full installation of the proposed maintenance sensors. The pilot would be owned by the reliability engineering group, reporting before the March capital review, and the decision on full installation held until the pilot results have been reported.

The evidence base is the plant's own maintenance record. Over 12 months, the records show 1114 h of unplanned downtime across the 260 pumps, with bearing failures accounting for 46% of the downtime hours. The case for the sensors rests on that bearing share, because a sensor set earns its cost only where the failures it detects early are the failures the plant actually has.

In a vendor trial on a comparable unit, the sensors cut downtime by 23%. The 23% is, however, a vendor figure and was not measured at this plant; it shows what the sensors achieved on another unit, and the pilot would convert it into a figure meaningful for this one. A sensor set for all 260 pumps is quoted at $413k installed, plus $78k per year, against $33k for the pilot over three months, so the pilot costs a small part of full installation while buying the plant's own downtime figure before the full sum is committed. Spare-part lead times are unchanged by the sensors, and no part of the case rests on faster repair.
